chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Mada'ini, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I not tell you about the noblest of moral traits?' I said: 'Yes.' He said:
Pardoning people, for a man to console his brother with his property, and to mention Allah abundantly.

key_terms.مَكَارِمُ الْأَخْلَاقِ: Noblest of moral traits / virtues of character

ai.seo_question: What are the noblest moral traits according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies forgiveness, financial solidarity, and constant dhikr as the essence of noble character, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating spiritual piety with social ethics. This triad underscores that true nobility (*makarim*) is not merely internal devotion but is manifested through tangible generosity and patience in interpersonal relations, a concept central to the Imams' teachings on moral perfection.

en.basel-kadem: 3.	We were told by muy father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from his father, from Nadr bin Suwayd, from Qasem bin Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Mada’ini, that he said: Abu Abdillah (a.s.) said to me: 'Shall I not tell you about the noblest of moral traits?' I said: 'Sure.' He said:
'Pardoning people, for a man to console his brother with his property and to mention Allah abundantly.'
